scenes.text: Day one in Germany. Everyone around you speaks German: the letters, the doctor, the announcements on the train. And the next language course? It's full.

More than one point four million Ukrainians now live in Germany, next to almost a million Syrians and hundreds of thousands of people from Iraq and Afghanistan. And this year, up to a hundred and thirty thousand people get no new place in a state integration course.
New to Germany? Don't be afraid. I've got you!
Strudli Lernen is made by immigrants, for immigrants. It's free, it runs on any phone, and it explains German in your own language.

scenes.title: German, explained in your language
scenes.text: It starts with the words you need this week. Every screen speaks your language, one tap switches between Ukrainian and English, and the stories are always one tap away.

scenes.title: Learn the article with the word
scenes.text: Each word comes with a photo, its translation and the right article, coloured for der, die and das.

scenes.title: German, like going to the cinema
bullets: Every word lights up as it is spoken
scenes.text: Then the heart of Strudli: animated stories, under Stories. A calm narrator reads a painted fairy tale, every word lights up the moment it is spoken, and the picture slowly comes to life.

scenes.title: Meaning in this exact sentence
bullets: sie = she or they, by context
scenes.text: Tap any word, and the story pauses to show what it means in exactly this sentence.

scenes.title: Not clear? Ask Strudli
bullets: A fresh example at A1 to A2
scenes.text: Stuck on a whole sentence? Tap Ask Strudli under the subtitles. Strudli himself explains it simply: the translation, the key words, the grammar, and a fresh example.
scenes.altText: Stuck on a whole sentence? Tap Ask Strudli under the subtitles. When the AI is not reachable, learners still get the human-checked translation, never an error.

scenes.title: A sentence from a letter? Ask Strudli
scenes.text: And for real life: paste a sentence from a letter or a sign, and Strudli explains it in your own language. Here, a line from a typical appointment letter.

scenes.title: 150 phrases for day one
scenes.text: For real life, there are a hundred and fifty phrases, for the Jobcenter, the doctor or the Kita, each recorded as one natural sentence.

scenes.title: Strudli Arena
scenes.text: And to make it stick, the Strudli Arena turns new words into a quick game show.

scenes.title: Your progress stays yours
scenes.text: Progress stays private on your phone, and an optional account without e-mail keeps it on every device.
Today, Strudli explains German in Ukrainian and English. Next come Arabic, Turkish and Farsi, with more levels and more stories.
Strudli Lernen. From immigrants, for immigrants. Willkommen in Deutschland.
